reason: The cited MD simulation evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the premise that melting point decreases with grain size from 3.6 to 2.0 nm, but it does not provide evidence for the proposed mechanistic roles of surface energy or disrupted local SRO, nor does it address the specific ~3 nm threshold or the ~90–100 K predicted shift.
premises: Melting point of nanocrystalline CoCrFeNiMn decreases with grain size from 3.6 to 2.0 nm
Surface energy and disrupted local SRO govern the size-dependent melting depression
Particles below ~3 nm exhibit more pronounced melting point depression due to high surface-to-volume ratios
The relationship holds for CoCrFeNiMn HEA nanoparticles in the ~2–4 nm size range
